q8.answer: Each customer's count lives in one Redis key, rl:{customerId}:{windowIndex}, so all gateway instances read and increment the same number. Old counts are removed by a 60-second expiry that is set only when the key is first created, so each counter disappears about a minute after its window starts.

q9.answer: The budget does not recover gradually. It resets at the next clock-minute boundary, because the window index comes from Redis server time and a new minute starts a new counter key at zero.

q10.answer: The check and the increment run as one atomic Lua script inside Redis, so two instances cannot both read 99 and both proceed. Whichever script runs first takes the last slot and the other is rejected. This relies on a single primary; a failover can lose a few recent counts, which the design accepts.

q11.answer: Redis computes the milliseconds until the current window ends, using its own server time, and returns that value to the gateway. The gateway rounds it up to whole seconds and uses a minimum of 1 for Retry-After.

q12.answer: The design makes one store call per request with no retry step, so a failed call fails open, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and the next request tries the store again. The client receives no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers in that case. I did not decide whether a retry should happen within the same request.
